name: Shalmai
overview: Shalmai was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role is specifically noted in the book of Ezra, highlighting his involvement in the religious duties associated with the temple. There are no additional personal details recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shalmai appears as a proper name in Scripture without a provided meaning or title significance. It is simply recorded as his given name in Ezra 2:26.
familyAndRelationships: Shalmai is identified as a descendant of Levi, indicating his Levitical heritage and connection to the priestly tribe. Beyond this tribal affiliation, Scripture does not provide further family relationships or genealogical details about him.
scriptureSignificance: Shalmai's significance lies in his role as a temple servant from the tribe of Levi during the post-exilic period. His mention in Ezra underscores the restoration of temple worship and the reestablishment of Levitical duties following the return from Babylonian captivity. As a temple servant, Shalmai contributed to the spiritual renewal and continuity of God's covenant community in Israel.
